placements.role: Planetary roller screws and harmonic reducers need high-precision grinding tools to mass-produce, and those tools are still dominated by a few European and Japanese makers; machine-tool availability can therefore cap component capacity expansion and the whole humanoid ramp trajectory. Klingelnberg makes precision bevel and cylindrical gear grinding, cutting and inspection machine tools used to manufacture the high-precision gear and flexspline profiles inside harmonic and cycloidal reducers; one of the few remaining listed pure-plays in gear-grinding machine tools now that Gleason and Liebherr-Verzahntechnik are private and Reishauer and Kapp Niles have stayed private.

business_summary: Klingelnberg AG is a Swiss precision machine-tool group headquartered in Zurich, listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange since 20 June 2018 (ticker KLIN, ISIN CH0420462266, 8,840,000 registered shares of CHF 5.00 nominal value). The group is organized in four divisions: Oerlikon Bevel Gear Technology (cutting, grinding, lapping and testing machines for bevel gears), HOFLER Cylindrical Gear Technology (cylindrical gear grinding machines and roll testing equipment), KLINGELNBERG Precision Measuring Centers (measuring systems for gears and rotationally symmetric components) and AIKTEC Digital Solutions (software). For fiscal year 2024/25 (ended 31 March 2025) the group reported net sales from goods and services of EUR 309.1 million (EUR 309,069 thousand), the highest in company history, up EUR 5.6 million from EUR 303.5 million in FY2023/24. Operating result (EBIT) was EUR 16.2 million (5.2% of net sales), down from EUR 25.1 million (8.3%) a year earlier, a decline the company attributes primarily to the absence of one-off flood-related payments booked in the prior year (the group's 14 July 2021 flood disaster). Net profit was EUR 10.0 million (EUR 9,985 thousand), down from EUR 17.2 million; basic EPS was EUR 1.13. Cash flow from operating activities was EUR 19.0 million (EUR 18,970 thousand) and cash flow from investing activities was EUR -12.5 million, for a company-defined free cash flow (CFO+CFI) of EUR 6.5 million (EUR 6,494 thousand). Net debt was EUR 25.6 million (EUR 25,614 thousand) and the equity ratio was 51.2% on total equity of EUR 143.4 million and total assets of EUR 280.1 million. Order intake was EUR 249.9 million (down 19.7% year over year) and the order backlog fell EUR 59.3 million to EUR 208.2 million. About 51.9% of sales were generated in Asia-Pacific and 30.0% in EMEA. Source: Klingelnberg AG Annual Report 2024/25 (fiscal year ended 31 March 2025, Swiss GAAP FER, published 24 June 2025), https://klingelnberg.com/fileadmin/Investors/Annual_Report_2024_25_final.pdf.

exposure_summary.narrative: One ACTIVE placement on the humanoid-actuators chain: precision-machine-tools (position 4 of the chain, the money corner, heat UNDISCOVERED, bottleneck CHOKE_POINT). Klingelnberg is not a maker of humanoid actuators, harmonic drives or reducers itself; its Oerlikon bevel-gear and HOFLER cylindrical-gear grinding, cutting, lapping and measuring machines are capital equipment that reducer and gear-component makers must buy to machine the single-digit-micron flexspline and gear profiles harmonic and cycloidal reducers require. The chain's own heat evidence documents a Chinese precision-reducer maker that had to redesign machine-tool structure, lead-screw guide rails and control system and build its own 7-axis 5-linkage grinder because no existing equipment could make its part, i.e. grinding capability rather than order intake sets how fast reducer capacity can scale. The chain's capture rationale also discounts this link from its 85+ anchor precisely because the strongest specialists, Kapp Niles and Reishauer, are private, so Klingelnberg's listed exposure is the residual, diluted inside its broader gear-machine-tool revenue. No humanoid-robot, harmonic-drive, reducer-industry or robotics-customer revenue is disclosed anywhere in Klingelnberg's own reporting; the placement rests on Klingelnberg's general precision gear-grinding and measuring machine-tool product category, not on a disclosed segment, customer, or order tied to humanoid robotics.
